questions.title: Which national team will win the first UEFA Nations League match between the Republic of Ireland and Israel in September 2026?
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : UEFA's official match result or reliable contemporaneous reporting of the first Nations League match between these teams in September 2026. Resolution : Resolve when the match finishes, using the final score. If neither team wins, resolve to a draw. Accepted Answer Format : The winning national team's name, or the result designation if the match is drawn.
questions.current_reasoning: Calibrated 2026-09-25 correction from fresh pre-match reporting (The Guardian, Sports Mole, LiveScore, Times of Israel, Al Jazeera Sept 25). Yesterday's shift to Israel 0.43 overreacted to MD1 and priced in an adopted Israeli crowd in Debrecen, whereas The Guardian (Sept 25) reports the neutral Hungarian stands are likely to be empty in an eerie, subdued atmosphere. Furthermore, Israel sits 76th in FIFA rankings (20 places below Ireland), has won only 2 of its last 8 internationals (Albania, Moldova), lost 3-1 in Linz after playing 35+ minutes down to 10 men, and misses both suspended goalscorer Sayed Abu Farchi (red card for gun-gesture celebration) and injured defensive trio Stav Lemkin, Itay Rotman, and Or Blorian. While Ireland remains depleted (Nathan Collins, Evan Ferguson, Josh Cullen, Jamie McGrath, Mikey Johnston, Jack Taylor out), flat in Kosovo, and distracted politically (Jason Knight publicly opposed playing though a boycott is not expected), Ireland was 8 matches unbeaten prior to Thursday, retains Caoimhin Kelleher and in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott, and both Sports Mole and LiveScore predict a 1-1 draw. Neutral-venue low-scoring Dixon-Coles modeling pulls Israel back 0.43 -> 0.37, lifts Draw 0.31 -> 0.33, and restores Republic of Ireland 0.26 -> 0.30.

local_articles.title: Pressure to boycott Israel game grows as Ireland preparations stall
local_articles.snippet: The Ireland team’s news conference and training session the day before its first Nations League game against Israel have been delayed as pressure to boycott the matches grows. Journalists in Debrecen, Hungary – where Israel’s “home” game is to be played Sunday – were left waiting Saturday after being told the news conference was being pushed back until after training. That was 15 minutes before it was supposed to begin. Training was also significantly delayed, however, with Irish broadcaster RTE reporting the players were still in their hotel more than two hours after the training session was supposed to begin. RTE reported that some players had decided they did not want to play the games. “And if they stay to their stated ambition that they have to be all in it together, if one or more want to be out, maybe they will all be out,” reporter Tony O’Donoghue told RTE Radio 1. questions.title: Which country's representative office in Ramallah will have its diplomats stripped of their Israeli-issued diplomatic status in September 2026?
questions.background: Foreign governments maintain representative offices to conduct diplomatic relations with the Palestinian Authority.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public announcements by Israel's Foreign Ministry, corroborated by reliable contemporaneous news reporting. Resolution Conditions : Resolve to the country whose diplomats at its representative office in Ramallah are formally announced to have had their Israeli-issued diplomatic status revoked during September 2026. The announcement of revocation is sufficient; implementation need not be independently verified. Accepted Answer Format : The country's name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-09-24 reassessment driven by new Al Jazeera and Times of Israel reporting (Sept 24) on West Bank settlement trade bans. No Israeli Foreign Ministry revocation of Ramallah diplomats has been announced yet through Sept 24 (Netanyahu was in New York addressing UNGA today), while ToI confirmed Norway already shuttered its al-Ram mission in Aug 2024. Crucially, Al Jazeera (Sept 24) revealed that the Netherlands brought a sweeping national ban into legal force TWO days ago on September 22—prohibiting the import, purchase, sale, facilitating services, and circumvention of Israeli settlement goods through Europe's key trade gateway—and Israel's Foreign Trade Administration head Roey Fisher explicitly singled out Spain and the Netherlands today as Europe's only effective boycotts. Unlike Spain (Jerusalem Consulate General, not Ramallah), the Netherlands operates a Representative Office in Ramallah, creating an acute, immediate retaliation trigger as Netanyahu returns from UNGA ahead of Sept 27. Meanwhile, Al Jazeera confirms Canada's pledged Sept 8 measures have still not entered into force 16 days after announcement (with no Israeli move against Canada yet, unlike Israel's 24-hour retaliation against the UK on Sept 9), though Canada remains a near co-favorite given Sept 9 Reuters cabinet-discussion reports flagging Canada's Ramallah office. Surging Netherlands sharply (0.06 -> 0.36), pulling Canada back from over-concentrated pre-announcement level (0.52 -> 0.34), trimming Ireland (0.16 -> 0.12; Occupied Territories Bill + acute Sept 23-27 bilateral friction), Denmark (0.05 -> 0.04), and Poland (0.05 -> 0.03), with 0.11 residual across Portugal, Finland, South Africa, Brazil, and others.
